quotes.quote: To derive phenogroups using the 5120 features extracted using the CODE-CNN model, K-means clustering was applied in the CODE data set using all 5120 features, without any further dimensionality reduction.
Survival analysis for the 3 phenogroups was first performed for the CODE data set and then in the 5 external validation data sets (UKB, Whitehall II, ELSA-Brasil, SaMi-Trop, and BIDMC).

G1.rationale: The principal result is produced by a computational pipeline (feature extraction, K-means clustering, survival analysis) that can be re-run on deposited ECG data.

quotes.quote: In these adjusted analyses, phenogroup B (highest mortality) had a 1.2-fold increase in long-term mortality compared with phenogroup A (HR, 1.20 [95% CI, 1.17–1.23]; P <0.0001; Table S3 ).

G2.rationale: The paper explicitly reports an adjusted hazard ratio as a principal quantitative result, with a clear endpoint (long-term mortality) and effect size.

quotes.quote: The São Paulo-Minas Gerais Tropical Medicine Research Center (SaMi-Trop) cohort was made openly available ( https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.4905618 ).
The Clinical Outcomes in Digital Electrocardiography (CODE)-15% cohort was also made openly available ( https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.4916206 ).

G3.rationale: The deposit listing for Zenodo 4905618 contains exams.csv and exams.zip, which likely include raw ECG waveforms and metadata for the SaMi-Trop cohort, but the paper does not explicitly state that these files are the exact inputs for the adjusted HR target; the CODE cohort (derivation) is not listed in the deposit.

quotes.quote: Twelve-lead ECGs were preprocessed by removing the baseline drift and resampling to 400 Hz. Zero padding resulted in a signal with 4096 samples for each lead for a 10-second recording, which is used as input to the NN model.

The CODE data set was previously used to train a CNN to detect 6 common ECG abnormalities (first-degree atrioventricular block, right bundle branch block, left bundle branch block, sinus bradycardia, atrial fibrillation, and sinus tachycardia), as previously described.

To derive phenogroups using the 5120 features extracted using the CODE-CNN model, K-means clustering was applied in the CODE data set using all 5120 features, without any further dimensionality reduction.
Cox proportional hazards regression modeling was used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) for mortality while correcting for other known variables.

G4.rationale: The methods for preprocessing, feature extraction, clustering, and survival analysis are described in sufficient detail to implement, though some details (e.g., exact covariates) are in Supplemental Methods.

quotes.quote: The Keras framework with a TensorFlow backend was used for NN training and inference.

G5.rationale: The methods rely on open-source software (Keras, TensorFlow, scikit-learn) and no proprietary software is required.

specification.exact_target: Adjusted hazard ratio for long-term mortality comparing phenogroup B versus phenogroup A in the CODE derivation cohort: HR, 1.20 [95% CI, 1.17–1.23]; P <0.0001
specification.blind_target: The adjusted hazard ratio for long-term mortality comparing phenogroup B to phenogroup A in the CODE derivation cohort, after adjusting for known covariates.
specification.target_location: Results, Survival Analysis section, and Table S3

location_quotes.quote: In these adjusted analyses, phenogroup B (highest mortality) had a 1.2-fold increase in long-term mortality compared with phenogroup A (HR, 1.20 [95% CI, 1.17–1.23]; P <0.0001; Table S3 ).

method_quotes.quote: Twelve-lead ECGs were preprocessed by removing the baseline drift and resampling to 400 Hz. Zero padding resulted in a signal with 4096 samples for each lead for a 10-second recording, which is used as input to the NN model.

The CODE data set was previously used to train a CNN to detect 6 common ECG abnormalities (first-degree atrioventricular block, right bundle branch block, left bundle branch block, sinus bradycardia, atrial fibrillation, and sinus tachycardia), as previously described.
In a transfer learning–based approach, the final classification layer of the model was removed (Figure 1 ), and the output of 5120 NN-derived ECG features is used to cluster the subjects.

To derive phenogroups using the 5120 features extracted using the CODE-CNN model, K-means clustering was applied in the CODE data set using all 5120 features, without any further dimensionality reduction.
Cox proportional hazards regression modeling was used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) for mortality while correcting for other known variables.

specification.input_notes: The deposit (Zenodo 4905618) contains exams.csv and exams.zip, which likely include ECG waveforms and metadata for the SaMi-Trop cohort. However, the target adjusted HR is for the CODE derivation cohort, which is not in this deposit. The CODE cohort data are not openly available; only the CODE-15% subset is available (Zenodo 4916206). Thus, the required inputs for the exact target are not fully deposited.

specification.comparison_metric: The observed hazard ratio and confidence interval from re-analysis will be compared to the reported values.
specification.numerical_agreement_criterion: Scalars within displayed rounding bin: HR within 0.01, CI bounds within 0.01, p-value at reported precision (<0.0001).
specification.specification_gaps: The exact set of covariates adjusted for in the Cox model is not fully specified in the main text; details are in Supplemental Methods. The CODE cohort data are not openly available, so the exact target cannot be reproduced without access.
